newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian traffic hit by farmers tax protest.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian traffic hit by farmers tax protest.

text.p: Hungarian farmers angered by tax changes blocked roads with thousands of tractors, ploughs and trucks at 70 places across the country on Monday, delaying traffic for hours, police said.
Organisers pledged to continue with the protests for at least two more days unless the government rescinded all the tax changes.

"We will not even talk to the government (about ending the protests) until all the new laws are suspended," Zsuzsa Sinkovicz, a member of the organising committee, said at a roadblock in this central Hungarian farm town.
The farmers are protesting against the end of an exception from social security contributions as of January 1 and new requirements to provide document for taxation purposes.
National police spokeswoman Eva Kiss said about 4,200 vehicles and up to 7,000 people took part in the demonstrations in eight of Hungary's 19 counties, mostly in the less developed east.
Kiss said that there were no incidents although cars queued for several kilometres in some places.
In Kiskoros, the centre of the protest, one of the main roads to Budapest was blocked by 500 vehicles forming a five-km-long line. It took hours for cars to get to the next village.
Traffic on Highway 5 which links the Balkans and Turkey to western Europe was also delayed.
Highway 3, a key western link, was blocked at Gyongyos, while cars queued for several kilometres on Highway 4, a key east-west route, Hungarian radio reported.

Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said earlier that the government was prepared to modify the new tax scheme but would not reinstate the social security exceptions for farmers or eliminate requirements to document expenses.
Making an exception would create unequal taxes for farmers and non-farmers and would jeopardise Hungary's finances while the documentation was needed to avoid abuse, Medgyessy said.
Farmers said the government was trying to balance its books on their backs.

"Gyula (Horn), don't try to recover from us the billions your government wasted," one placard taped to the top of a tractor said, referring to the prime minister. Another placard said: "We want to farm, not do bookkeeping."
